title: Jest Examples
description: Small Jest examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Your first Jest test
examples.description: Jest runs a test function and reports whether its checks pass. expect gives the actual value; a matcher states the expected result.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("adds two prices", () => { expect(2 + 3).toBe(5); });

examples.title: Compare object contents
examples.description: toEqual checks values inside objects. This is different from checking whether two names refer to the exact same object.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("book fields", () => { expect({ title: "Moon" }).toEqual({ title: "Moon" }); });

examples.title: Check lists and text
examples.description: A length check and a containment check answer different questions about a list.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("reading list", () => { const books = ["Moon", "Ocean"]; expect(books).toHaveLength(2); expect(books).toContain("Moon"); });

examples.title: Check an error
examples.description: Pass a function to toThrow so Jest can call it and catch the error.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("rejects bad age", () => { const reject = () => { throw new Error("Bad age"); }; expect(reject).toThrow("Bad age"); });

examples.title: Set up fresh state
examples.description: beforeEach runs before each test in its scope. Use it to prepare fresh mutable data.

examples.title: Use a mock function
examples.description: jest.fn makes a function that records calls. A mock can stand in for a small dependency.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("saves a score", () => { const save = jest.fn(); save(8); expect(save).toHaveBeenCalledWith(8); });

examples.title: Choose a mock return value
examples.description: A mock can return a chosen value so the code under test has predictable input.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("reads a name", () => { const getName = jest.fn().mockReturnValue("Asha"); expect(getName()).toBe("Asha"); });

examples.title: Wait for a promise
examples.description: An async test can await a promise. resolves checks the value with which it finishes successfully.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("loads a score", async () => { await expect(Promise.resolve(8)).resolves.toBe(8); });

examples.title: Check promise rejection
examples.description: rejects checks a promise that fails. It is useful for an expected error path.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("reports missing data", async () => { await expect(Promise.reject(new Error("Missing"))).rejects.toThrow("Missing"); });

examples.title: Run a table of cases
examples.description: test.each runs a test with each row of data. A row contains inputs and expected output.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test.each([[2, 4], [3, 6], [0, 0]])("double %i is %i", (input, expected) => { expect(input * 2).toBe(expected); });

examples.title: Control a timer
examples.description: Fake timers let a test move time forward without really waiting. Restore real timers when the test ends.
examples.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("reminder runs later", () => { jest.useFakeTimers(); try { const remind = jest.fn(); setTimeout(remind, 1000); jest.advanceTimersByTime(1000); expect(remind).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1); } finally { jest.useRealTimers(); } });

examples.title: Review snapshots thoughtfully
examples.description: A snapshot stores an expected structure. Review changes instead of accepting a new snapshot blindly.
